prerequisites: Second study section reached (at least 42 ECTS points from the first study section must be proven).
Familiarity with mathematical notation, basics of set theory (functions, relations).

learning_outcomes.text: explain fundamental concepts, terms, and relationships in the sub-fields of Formal Languages, Automata Theory, Computability Theory, and Complexity Theory
independently conduct simple proofs and apply their problem-solving competence in doing so
differentiate the capabilities of formal language description methods (Chomsky Hierarchy)
describe formal languages independently using the presented methods
describe important abstract computational models and know that there are limits to computability
name important historical milestones in computer science and recognize their influence on current and future development

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts: Alphabets, Words, Formal Languages, Grammars, Chomsky Hierarchy, Word Problem
Regular Languages: deterministic and non-deterministic finite automata, powerset construction, regular expressions, minimization, Pumping Lemma, Myhill-Nerode Theorem, closure properties
Context-Free Languages: Normal forms, Pumping Lemma, closure properties, CYK algorithm, Pushdown Automata
Context-Sensitive and Type-0 Languages: linearly bounded automata, Turing machines
Abstract computing and programming models: Turing machines, Abacus machines
Decision problems: Halting problem, Reduction principle, Rice's Theorem
